Subharmonic Injection: From the Impulse Train to ×N Multiplication (ILCM / ILFM)

Prerequisites: paper_003 ([P3] Sec. IV impulse train, Eq.(19)–(23), generalized Adler), paper_004 (the M:N time-synchronous average of [P4] Eq.(28)–(30)), injection_locked_division (the other half of the duality: division rides on the ISF's NNN-th harmonic), injection_locking_noise (a locked oscillator is a first-order PLL, corner =−Ω′(θss)=-\Omega'(\theta_{ss})=−Ω′(θss␀​)) | Next: lab_40_subharmonic_injection (independent simulation), sampling_pll, clock_chain_budget

What this page answers:

  1. Fire freff_{ref}fref​ pulses into an oscillator running at f0=Nfreff_0=N f_{ref}f0​=Nfref​ — why does it lock? On whose harmonics? Why can a pure sinusoid at f0/Nf_0/Nf0​/N not lock?
  2. Why is the lock range ∝1/N\propto 1/N∝1/N? How do the two routes — the [P4] Fourier average and the [P3] impulse-train arithmetic — agree term by term?
  3. How much phase does each pulse "pull back" — what is the realignment factor β\betaβ, what sets it, how large may it be, how many pulses to settle?
  4. How is the phase noise of the locked output budgeted: reference ×N2\times N^2×N2, own noise shaped by a first-order discrete-time loop, closed-form output jitter, where the reference spur comes from?
  5. Design knobs: pulse width, ring vs LC, NNN, β\betaβ; how does an ILCM compare with a classic PLL and a sub-sampling PLL?

Physical intuition (conclusion first): an injection-locked clock multiplier (ILCM) is not a "multiplier circuit" — it is an oscillator that already runs at f0≈Nfreff_0\approx N f_{ref}f0​≈Nfref​ and gets kicked by a reference pulse once every NNN of its own periods. One kick = one ISF phase step Δϕ=Γ~(θ) qinj\Delta\phi=\tilde\Gamma(\theta)\,q_{inj}Δϕ=Γ~(θ)qinj​; between pulses the oscillator free-runs, its phase drifts with the detuning and random-walks with noise. Locking = each kick exactly repays the phase owed over those NNN periods; noise suppression = each kick pulls the accumulated random phase back by a fraction β\betaβ. What makes the lock possible is the injection waveform's own NNN-th harmonic (the oscillator's ISF fundamental only hears things near f0f_0f0​) — the mirror image of the divider (ILFD): division rides on ISF harmonics, multiplication on injection harmonics.

Scope of this page: advanced design page. The text, equations and footnotes of [P3] Sec. IV (p.2112) and [P4] Sec. IV (p.2129) were re-read from the enlarged PDF pages word by word (Section 0). [P4] writes out the closed form Eq.(30) only for the superharmonic case (M=1M=1M=1, a sinusoid at NωoscN\omega_{osc}Nωosc​); for the subharmonic (multiplier) side the paper gives only the general statement and footnote 10 — this page derives the multiplier closed form from Eq.(29) step by step, derives the 1/N1/N1/N law and the realignment factor from the discrete arithmetic of [P3] Sec. IV, and reconciles the two routes. Section 4, "putting noise into the discrete loop", is the textbook-level ILCM / realignment result (external literature, not in the site's 5 PDFs; two verified classics are listed at the end), derived here and checked term by term against this page's own Monte-Carlo. Every model is a phase-only, weak-injection pedagogical toy.

0. What the papers say — and do not say (verbatim check of [P3] p.2112 and [P4] p.2129)​

0.1 [P3] Sec. IV "Locking to an Impulse Train" (p.2112)​

paper_003 already teaches this section step by step: an ideal parallel LC fed by a train of current impulses of period Tinj≡2π/ωinjT_{inj}\equiv2\pi/\omega_{inj}Tinj​≡2π/ωinj​, each dumping a fixed charge qinjq_{inj}qinj​ (Fig. 3(a); the paper takes qinj≥0q_{inj}\ge0qinj​≥0 by convention, with the sign selecting Fig. 3(b) speed-up or Fig. 3(c) slow-down; the state-space impulse arrows in the figure are deliberately enlarged, not to scale). Four core equations:

Δϕ=±qinjqmax  (19),Δϕ2π=−ΔTT0=Δωωinj  (20),Δω=ΔϕTinj=±1Tinjqinjqmax  (21),Iinj=2qinjTinj  (23)\Delta\phi=\pm\frac{q_{inj}}{q_{max}}\ \ (19),\qquad \frac{\Delta\phi}{2\pi}=-\frac{\Delta T}{T_0}=\frac{\Delta\omega}{\omega_{inj}}\ \ (20),\qquad \Delta\omega=\frac{\Delta\phi}{T_{inj}}=\pm\frac{1}{T_{inj}}\frac{q_{inj}}{q_{max}}\ \ (21),\qquad I_{inj}=\frac{2q_{inj}}{T_{inj}}\ \ (23)Δϕ=±qmax​qinj​​  (19),2πΔϕ​=−T0​ΔT​=ωinj​Δω​  (20),Δω=Tinj​Δϕ​=±Tinj​1​qmax​qinj​​  (21),Iinj​=Tinj​2qinj​​  (23)

The text states that for each qinjq_{inj}qinj​ there is an injection period TinjT_{inj}Tinj​ that makes the next impulse always land at the same place on the waveform, so the period is sustainedly lengthened or shortened while the amplitude never changes. That sentence carries two footnotes, both directly relevant here:

  • footnote 7 (verified verbatim): the injection can also happen "every MMM periods (MMM a positive integer) … corresponding to subharmonic locking" — this is the starting point of this page: replace "one pulse per period" with "one pulse every NNN periods". The paper gives only this sentence; the arithmetic is completed in Section 2.
  • footnote 8: injections that no longer preserve the amplitude (pulses not at the zero crossing) are left to the companion paper [P4] Sec. III-B — i.e. the APF / amplitude modulation of [P4] (paper_004). The phase-only model of this page ignores it; Section 3 points out where it bites.

0.2 [P4] Sec. IV "Superharmonic and Subharmonic Injections" (p.2129)​

[P4] redefines the relative phase as (Eq.(28), M,NM,NM,N positive coprime integers)

φ(t)≡MN ωinjt+θ(t)\varphi(t)\equiv\frac{M}{N}\,\omega_{inj}t+\theta(t)φ(t)≡NM​ωinj​t+θ(t)

and obtains the generalized pulling equation (Eq.(29))

dθdt=ω0−MNωinj+1NTinj∫NTinjΓ~ ⁣(MNωinjt+θ)iinj(t) dt.\frac{d\theta}{dt}=\omega_0-\frac{M}{N}\omega_{inj}+\frac{1}{NT_{inj}}\int_{NT_{inj}}\tilde\Gamma\!\left(\frac{M}{N}\omega_{inj}t+\theta\right)i_{inj}(t)\,dt .dtdθ​=ω0​−NM​ωinj​+NTinj​1​∫NTinj​​Γ~(NM​ωinj​t+θ)iinj​(t)dt.

The text then says that this M:NM{:}NM:N framework covers any rational ratio Mωinj=NωoscM\omega_{inj}=N\omega_{osc}Mωinj​=Nωosc​ under lock, and that a Fourier series shows at a glance that locking "requires the MMMth-multiple harmonics of the injection to interact with the NNNth-multiple harmonics of the oscillator's ISF"; it also notes that relative phases 2π/N2\pi/N2π/N apart are indistinguishable, so Ω(θ)\Omega(\theta)Ω(θ) has period 2π/N2\pi/N2π/N. Then — only for a superharmonic sinusoidal injection (at the NNNth superharmonic, amplitude IinjI_{inj}Iinj​) — the closed form is written out (Eq.(30)):

Ω(θ)=12Iinj∣Γ~N∣cos⁡ ⁣(Nθ+∠Γ~N).\Omega(\theta)=\frac{1}{2}I_{inj}\vert\tilde\Gamma_N\vert\cos\!\big(N\theta+\angle\tilde\Gamma_N\big).Ω(θ)=21​Iinj​∣Γ~N​∣cos(Nθ+∠Γ~N​).

What the paper does not write: a subharmonic (M≠1M\neq1M=1, multiplier) closed form for a sinusoid or a pulse. Footnote 10 honestly explains why: for M≠1M\neq1M=1 the higher-order harmonics the injection needs are often generated by mixing inside the oscillator, a nonlinear phenomenon "not explicitly captured by our framework", partly handled by the model of its reference [25] (which was used to design subharmonic injection-locked frequency multipliers). This page therefore assumes the injection waveform itself carries enough NNN-th harmonic (that is what a pulse generator is for), so that the first-order average of Eq.(29) applies directly, without relying on internal mixing outside the framework.

Fractional lock range =0.05/(2π×20)=3.98×10−4=0.05/(2\pi\times20)=3.98\times10^{-4}=0.05/(2π×20)=3.98×10−4 = 398 ppm — two orders of magnitude below the PVT uncertainty of the free-running frequency (percent level). This is why real ILCMs almost always carry a frequency-tracking loop (FLL); Section 5.4 returns to it.
  4. One line of Python: 50e-15/1e-12/(20*200e-12)/(2*3.141592653589793)/1e6 → 1.9891.9891.989.

Step 4 (reconciling the two routes — they must agree exactly). The Fourier series of a delta train is qinjTinj[1+2∑k≥1cos⁡(kωinjt)]\frac{q_{inj}}{T_{inj}}\big[1+2\sum_{k\ge1}\cos(k\omega_{inj}t)\big]Tinj​qinj​​[1+2∑k≥1​cos(kωinj​t)]: I0=qinj/TinjI_0=q_{inj}/T_{inj}I0​=qinj​/Tinj​, all k≥1k\ge1k≥1 have ∣Ik∣=2qinj/Tinj\vert I_k\vert=2q_{inj}/T_{inj}∣Ik​∣=2qinj​/Tinj​ (k=1k=1k=1 is [P3] Eq.(23)), ∠Ik=0\angle I_k=0∠Ik​=0. Insert into the general formula of Section 1:

Ω(θ)=qinjTinj[Γ~dc+∑m≥1∣Γ~m∣cos⁡ ⁣(mθ+∠Γ~m)]=qinjTinj Γ~(θ)\Omega(\theta)=\frac{q_{inj}}{T_{inj}}\Big[\tilde\Gamma_{dc}+\sum_{m\ge1}\vert\tilde\Gamma_m\vert\cos\!\big(m\theta+\angle\tilde\Gamma_m\big)\Big]=\frac{q_{inj}}{T_{inj}}\,\tilde\Gamma(\theta)Ω(θ)=Tinj​qinj​​[Γ~dc​+m≥1∑​∣Γ~m​∣cos(mθ+∠Γ~m​)]=Tinj​qinj​​Γ~(θ)

— the Fourier sum reassembles the ISF as it is, which is precisely the map's "kick per unit time" qinjΓ~(θ)/Tinjq_{inj}\tilde\Gamma(\theta)/T_{inj}qinj​Γ~(θ)/Tinj​. For Γ=−sin⁡\Gamma=-\sinΓ=−sin: route 1 gives 12⋅2qinjTinj⋅1qmax=qinjqmaxTinj\tfrac12\cdot\frac{2q_{inj}}{T_{inj}}\cdot\frac{1}{q_{max}}=\frac{q_{inj}}{q_{max}T_{inj}}21​⋅Tinj​2qinj​​⋅qmax​1​=qmax​Tinj​qinj​​ = route 2 ✓. The two routes are two spellings of one identity: all harmonics of a delta train have equal weight, so "injection NNN-th harmonic × ISF fundamental" and "one kick ÷ NT0NT_0NT0​" are the same number.

Step 5 (finite pulse width). For a rectangular pulse of width τp\tau_pτp​ and area qinjq_{inj}qinj​, ∣Ik∣=2qinjTinj∣sinc(kfrefτp)∣\vert I_k\vert=\frac{2q_{inj}}{T_{inj}}\big\vert\mathrm{sinc}(k f_{ref}\tau_p)\big\vert∣Ik​∣=Tinj​2qinj​​​sinc(kfref​τp​)​ (sinc(x)=sin⁡(πx)/(πx)\mathrm{sinc}(x)=\sin(\pi x)/(\pi x)sinc(x)=sin(πx)/(πx)). The lock uses k=Nk=Nk=N, whose argument is Nfrefτp=f0τpNf_{ref}\tau_p=f_0\tau_pNfref​τp​=f0​τp​ — the pulse width is compared with the oscillation period, not the reference period. The same thing in the time domain: during the pulse the ISF argument advances 2πf0τp2\pi f_0\tau_p2πf0​τp​, the kick is the average of Γ~\tilde\GammaΓ~ over that span, and for −sin⁡-\sin−sin that is again ×sinc(f0τp)\times\mathrm{sinc}(f_0\tau_p)×sinc(f0​τp​). τp=10\tau_p=10τp​=10 ps: sinc(0.05)=0.99589\mathrm{sinc}(0.05)=0.99589sinc(0.05)=0.99589, ∣I20∣=25.00×0.99589=24.90 μ\vert I_{20}\vert=25.00\times0.99589=24.90\ \mu∣I20​∣=25.00×0.99589=24.90 μA, ωL=12×24.90×10−6×1012=1.245×107\omega_L=\tfrac12\times24.90\times10^{-6}\times10^{12}=1.245\times10^{7}ωL​=21​×24.90×10−6×1012=1.245×107 rad/s ⟹ 1.9811.9811.981 MHz (0.4% below the delta train).

3. Realignment factor β\betaβ: how much phase one pulse pulls back​

Linearize the per-pulse map. Put θk=θss+δθk\theta_k=\theta_{ss}+\delta\theta_kθk​=θss​+δθk​, Γ~(θss+δθ)≈Γ~(θss)+Γ~′(θss)δθ\tilde\Gamma(\theta_{ss}+\delta\theta)\approx\tilde\Gamma(\theta_{ss})+\tilde\Gamma'(\theta_{ss})\delta\thetaΓ~(θss​+δθ)≈Γ~(θss​)+Γ~′(θss​)δθ, and let the fixed-point condition cancel the constant:

δθk+1=δθk+qinjΓ~′(θss) δθk=(1−β) δθk, β≡−qinj Γ~′(θss) \delta\theta_{k+1}=\delta\theta_k+q_{inj}\tilde\Gamma'(\theta_{ss})\,\delta\theta_k=(1-\beta)\,\delta\theta_k,\qquad \boxed{\ \beta\equiv-q_{inj}\,\tilde\Gamma'(\theta_{ss})\ }δθk+1​=δθk​+qinj​Γ~′(θss​)δθk​=(1−β)δθk​, β≡−qinj​Γ~′(θss​) ​

β\betaβ = injected charge × ISF slope at the lock point, dimensionless (C × rad/C/rad ✓). It is "the fraction of the current phase error that one pulse pulls back": β=1\beta=1β=1 realigns in one step (an MDLL-style hard reset), β≪1\beta\ll1β≪1 pulls a little each time.

  • Stability: ∣1−β∣<1  ⟺  0<β<2\vert1-\beta\vert\lt1\iff0\lt\beta\lt2∣1−β∣<1⟺0<β<2. β>1\beta\gt1β>1 overshoots and swings back (alternating convergence); β≥2\beta\ge2β≥2 diverges. For weak injection β≪1\beta\ll1β≪1 the condition reduces to Γ~′(θss)<0\tilde\Gamma'(\theta_{ss})\lt0Γ~′(θss​)<0 — the same statement as the discrete stability in paper_003 and the continuous "Ω′(θ0)<0\Omega'(\theta_0)\lt0Ω′(θ0​)<0" of [P3] Eq.(38)–(39).
  • Settling: the error is ∝(1−β)k=ekln⁡(1−β)\propto(1-\beta)^k=e^{k\ln(1-\beta)}∝(1−β)k=ekln(1−β); 1/e1/e1/e needs ke=−1/ln⁡(1−β)≈1/βk_e=-1/\ln(1-\beta)\approx1/\betake​=−1/ln(1−β)≈1/β injections (β≪1\beta\ll1β≪1).
  • Relation to the continuous corner: pulling back β\betaβ every TinjT_{inj}Tinj​ ⟺ a restoring rate ωc=β/Tinj\omega_c=\beta/T_{inj}ωc​=β/Tinj​. Compare with the continuous limit of the map, Ω(θ)=qinjΓ~(θ)/Tinj\Omega(\theta)=q_{inj}\tilde\Gamma(\theta)/T_{inj}Ω(θ)=qinj​Γ~(θ)/Tinj​: −Ω′(θss)=−qinjΓ~′(θss)/Tinj=β/Tinj-\Omega'(\theta_{ss})=-q_{inj}\tilde\Gamma'(\theta_{ss})/T_{inj}=\beta/T_{inj}−Ω′(θss​)=−qinj​Γ~′(θss​)/Tinj​=β/Tinj​ ✓ — β/Tinj\beta/T_{inj}β/Tinj​ is the ωc=−Ω′(θss)\omega_c=-\Omega'(\theta_{ss})ωc​=−Ω′(θss​) of injection_locking_noise and the pull-in frequency of [P3] Eq.(40), restated in discrete time.

β\betaβ of the LC toy (Γ~=−sin⁡θ/qmax\tilde\Gamma=-\sin\theta/q_{max}Γ~=−sinθ/qmax​, Γ~′=−cos⁡θ/qmax\tilde\Gamma'=-\cos\theta/q_{max}Γ~′=−cosθ/qmax​):

β=qinjqmaxcos⁡θss=qinjqmax1−(Δω0ΔωL)2\beta=\frac{q_{inj}}{q_{max}}\cos\theta_{ss}=\frac{q_{inj}}{q_{max}}\sqrt{1-\Big(\frac{\Delta\omega_0}{\Delta\omega_L}\Big)^2}β=qmax​qinj​​cosθss​=qmax​qinj​​1−(ΔωL​Δω0​​)2​

(lock condition sin⁡θss=−Δω0/ΔωL\sin\theta_{ss}=-\Delta\omega_0/\Delta\omega_Lsinθss​=−Δω0​/ΔωL​, stable branch cos⁡θss>0\cos\theta_{ss}\gt0cosθss​>0). At zero detuning θss=0\theta_{ss}=0θss​=0 and β=qinj/qmax\beta=q_{inj}/q_{max}β=qinj​/qmax​; towards the edge of the lock range β\betaβ falls to zero along a circular arc — the same arc as ωc=ωL2−Δω2\omega_c=\sqrt{\omega_L^2-\Delta\omega^2}ωc​=ωL2​−Δω2​ in injection_locking_noise. A pleasant identity: for the LC at centre, β/Tinj=(qinj/qmax)/Tinj=ΔωL\beta/T_{inj}=(q_{inj}/q_{max})/T_{inj}=\Delta\omega_Lβ/Tinj​=(qinj​/qmax​)/Tinj​=ΔωL​ — the loop bandwidth (rad/s) equals the half lock range, the old first-order PLL / Adler rule, because the "maximum slope" and "maximum amplitude" of −sin⁡-\sin−sin are both 1.

Example 2 (β\betaβ and settling): qinj=50q_{inj}=50qinj​=50 fC, qmax=1q_{max}=1qmax​=1 pC, Δω0=0\Delta\omega_0=0Δω0​=0 ⟹ β=0.0500\beta=0.0500β=0.0500 (times sinc for the 10 ps pulse: 0.04980.04980.0498). ke=−1/ln⁡(0.95)=19.5k_e=-1/\ln(0.95)=19.5ke​=−1/ln(0.95)=19.5 injections = 19.5×419.5\times419.5×4 ns = 78 ns; 1/β=201/\beta=201/β=20 ✓. At detuning 0.5 ΔωL0.5\,\Delta\omega_L0.5ΔωL​, β=0.0433\beta=0.0433β=0.0433; at 0.95 ΔωL0.95\,\Delta\omega_L0.95ΔωL​ only 0.01560.01560.0156 — still locked, but almost no restoring force left. β/Tinj=0.05/4 ns=1.25×107\beta/T_{inj}=0.05/4\ \text{ns}=1.25\times10^{7}β/Tinj​=0.05/4 ns=1.25×107 rad/s = ΔωL\Delta\omega_LΔωL​ ✓.

Where on the waveform is the lock point? (an APF reminder) The LC's Γ=−sin⁡θ\Gamma=-\sin\thetaΓ=−sinθ is zero at θ=0\theta=0θ=0 (the voltage peak) with maximum slope. So at zero detuning the pulse lands exactly on the peak — no phase shift, maximum β\betaβ, but that is where the [P4] APF ∣Λ~∣\vert\tilde\Lambda\vert∣Λ~∣ is largest (ISF/APF quadrature, paper_004): each pulse kicks the amplitude, which then relaxes with τ0=2Q/ω0\tau_0=2Q/\omega_0τ0​=2Q/ω0​. The phase-only model cannot see this; for qinj≪qmaxq_{inj}\ll q_{max}qinj​≪qmax​ it is second order, for strong injection go back to the [P4] correction. Conversely, at the edge of the lock range the pulse lands on the zero crossing (∣Γ∣=1\vert\Gamma\vert=1∣Γ∣=1, Λ~≈0\tilde\Lambda\approx0Λ~≈0) — which is exactly how [P3] Fig. 3 is drawn: Fig. 3 depicts the edge of the lock range, not its centre.

Ring vs LC: whose β\betaβ is larger? (an honest calculation)​

Using the [P2] App. B triangular ISF construction (same as lab_39: two opposite-sign triangular pulses, height 1/f′1/f'1/f′, half-width 1/f′1/f'1/f′ rad, f′=ηNst/πf'=\eta N_{st}/\pif′=ηNst​/π; Nst=17N_{st}=17Nst​=17, η=0.75\eta=0.75η=0.75):

β\betaβ, same qinjq_{inj}qinj​, same qmax=1q_{max}=1qmax​=1 pCqinj/qmaxq_{inj}/q_{max}qinj​/qmax​qinj/qmaxq_{inj}/q_{max}qinj​/qmax​ (a tie)
β\betaβ, same qinj=1q_{inj}=1qinj​=1 fC, each with its own qmaxq_{max}qmax​10−310^{-3}10−3 (1 pC)0.1000.1000.100 (lab_32's qmax=CLVDD=10q_{max}=C_LV_{DD}=10qmax​=CL​VDD​=10 fC)

The conclusion has to be stated plainly: in this triangular construction the ring does not win by having a "steeper ISF" — h/w=(1/f′)/(1/f′)=1h/w=(1/f')/(1/f')=1h/w=(1/f′)/(1/f′)=1, the same as the peak slope of −sin⁡-\sin−sin, and ∣Γ∣max\vert\Gamma\vert_{max}∣Γ∣max​ is even smaller than the LC's (4× less lock range per qinjq_{inj}qinj​). What makes rings easy to realign in practice is a qmaxq_{max}qmax​ two orders of magnitude smaller (10 fF × 1 V = 10 fC vs pC-level for the LC): for the same 1 fC pulse, β\betaβ differs by 100×; β∼0.5\beta\sim0.5β∼0.5–111 is routine for a ring and nearly impossible for an LC (50 fC into a 10 fC node is qinj/qmax=5q_{inj}/q_{max}=5qinj​/qmax​=5, already outside the linear model). Two further ring features: (i) β\betaβ is constant across the whole flank, without the LC's arc that decays towards the edge (but it flips sign abruptly past the triangle tip); (ii) a pulse landing in the dead zone does nothing — so a ring ILCM's pulses must be aimed at the switching edge.

4. Noise: a first-order discrete-time loop (one update per Tinj=NT0T_{inj}=NT_0Tinj​=NT0​)​

4.1 Model and transfer functions​

Two noise sources: the oscillator's own white frequency noise (between pulses, i.e. over each TinjT_{inj}Tinj​, the phase random-walks with variance growth rate κ2\kappa^2κ2 [rad²/s], canonical κ2=0.125\kappa^2=0.125κ2=0.125 rad²/s, see diffusion_dictionary), and the phase error of the reference edges ψk\psi_kψk​ (in rad at freff_{ref}fref​). One rad of the reference is NNN rad at the output (same seconds, NNN times the angular frequency — clock_chain_budget rule 1), so the pulse pulls the oscillator towards NψkN\psi_kNψk​. Taking the phase just before each pulse, θk−\theta_k^-θk−​, as the state:

θk+=θk−−β(θk−−Nψk),θk+1−=θk++wk+1,Var[w]=σw2=κ2Tinj=κ2NT0\theta_k^+=\theta_k^--\beta\big(\theta_k^--N\psi_k\big),\qquad \theta_{k+1}^-=\theta_k^++w_{k+1},\qquad \mathrm{Var}[w]=\sigma_w^2=\kappa^2T_{inj}=\kappa^2NT_0θk+​=θk−​−β(θk−​−Nψk​),θk+1−​=θk+​+wk+1​,Var[w]=σw2​=κ2Tinj​=κ2NT0​

Combined: θk+1−=(1−β)θk−+βNψk+wk+1\theta_{k+1}^-=(1-\beta)\theta_k^-+\beta N\psi_k+w_{k+1}θk+1−​=(1−β)θk−​+βNψk​+wk+1​. Taking the zzz-transform (z=ej2πfTinjz=e^{j2\pi fT_{inj}}z=ej2πfTinj​):

Writing www as the first difference of the free-running random walk ϕosc\phi_{osc}ϕosc​, W=(1−z−1)ΦoscW=(1-z^{-1})\Phi_{osc}W=(1−z−1)Φosc​, gives

 Href(z)=β1−(1−β)z−1,Hosc(z)=1−z−11−(1−β)z−1,Sout(f)=∣Href∣2N2Sref(f)+∣Hosc∣2Sosc(f) \boxed{\ H_{ref}(z)=\frac{\beta}{1-(1-\beta)z^{-1}},\qquad H_{osc}(z)=\frac{1-z^{-1}}{1-(1-\beta)z^{-1}},\qquad S_{out}(f)=\vert H_{ref}\vert^2N^2S_{ref}(f)+\vert H_{osc}\vert^2S_{osc}(f)\ } Href​(z)=1−(1−β)z−1β​,Hosc​(z)=1−(1−β)z−11−z−1​,Sout​(f)=∣Href​∣2N2Sref​(f)+∣Hosc​∣2Sosc​(f) ​

(the reference path carries an extra pure delay z−1z^{-1}z−1 that leaves ∣Href∣\vert H_{ref}\vert∣Href​∣ unchanged; Sosc=2κ2/ω2S_{osc}=2\kappa^2/\omega^2Sosc​=2κ2/ω2 is the free-running single-sided 1/f21/f^21/f2 skirt, SrefS_{ref}Sref​ the reference's single-sided phase PSD at freff_{ref}fref​ [rad²/Hz]).

At low frequency x≡2πfTinj≪1x\equiv2\pi fT_{inj}\ll1x≡2πfTinj​≪1, z−1≈1−jxz^{-1}\approx1-jxz−1≈1−jx, so 1−(1−β)z−1≈β+j(1−β)x1-(1-\beta)z^{-1}\approx\beta+j(1-\beta)x1−(1−β)z−1≈β+j(1−β)x and 1−z−1≈jx1-z^{-1}\approx jx1−z−1≈jx:

4.4 Reference spur (the fingerprint of periodic realignment, first-order estimate)​

Locked but detuned (Δω0≠0\Delta\omega_0\neq0Δω0​=0), the steady-state phase is a sawtooth: linear drift Δω0Tinj\Delta\omega_0T_{inj}Δω0​Tinj​ between pulses, a jump back at each pulse. Peak-to-peak Δθpp=∣Δω0∣Tinj\Delta\theta_{pp}=\vert\Delta\omega_0\vert T_{inj}Δθpp​=∣Δω0​∣Tinj​. The kkk-th harmonic of a sawtooth has amplitude Δθpp/(πk)\Delta\theta_{pp}/(\pi k)Δθpp​/(πk), and for small-angle PM each sideband's power is (amplitude/2)², so

 spurk≈20log⁡10 ⁣(Δθpp2πk) dBc,spur1=20log⁡10 ⁣(∣Δf0∣fref) \boxed{\ \text{spur}_k\approx20\log_{10}\!\Big(\frac{\Delta\theta_{pp}}{2\pi k}\Big)\ \text{dBc},\qquad \text{spur}_1=20\log_{10}\!\Big(\frac{\vert\Delta f_0\vert}{f_{ref}}\Big)\ } spurk​≈20log10​(2πkΔθpp​​) dBc,spur1​=20log10​(fref​∣Δf0​∣​) ​

The second equality uses Δθpp=2πΔf0Tinj\Delta\theta_{pp}=2\pi\Delta f_0T_{inj}Δθpp​=2πΔf0​Tinj​. In the linearized form often quoted: the fixed-point condition linearized gives β ∣θss−θ0∣=∣Δω0∣Tinj\beta\,\vert\theta_{ss}-\theta_0\vert=\vert\Delta\omega_0\vert T_{inj}β∣θss​−θ0​∣=∣Δω0​∣Tinj​ (θ0\theta_0θ0​ the zero-kick phase), so Δθpp=β∣Δθ∣\Delta\theta_{pp}=\beta\vert\Delta\theta\vertΔθpp​=β∣Δθ∣ — the step at each pulse = β\betaβ × the offset of the lock point from the zero-kick point.

Example 4: Δf0=100\Delta f_0=100Δf0​=100 kHz, fref=250f_{ref}=250fref​=250 MHz ⟹ Δθpp=2π×105×4×10−9=2.51\Delta\theta_{pp}=2\pi\times10^{5}\times4\times10^{-9}=2.51Δθpp​=2π×105×4×10−9=2.51 mrad, spur1=20log⁡10(4×10−4)=−68.0\text{spur}_1=20\log_{10}(4\times10^{-4})=-68.0spur1​=20log10​(4×10−4)=−68.0 dBc (FFT of the sawtooth PM in the script: −67.95-67.95−67.95 dBc; at 2fref2f_{ref}2fref​ −73.97-73.97−73.97 vs theory −73.98-73.98−73.98 ✓). Δf0=10\Delta f_0=10Δf0​=10 kHz → −88-88−88 dBc; 1 MHz → −48-48−48 dBc. With β=0.05\beta=0.05β=0.05, a 100 kHz detuning corresponds to a lock point 50.350.350.3 mrad from the zero-kick point.

Honest label: this is a first-order estimate — it assumes a linear phase ramp within the interval and ignores direct coupling (feedthrough) of the pulse itself, APF-induced AM, pulse-width effects and nonlinear kicks. What it says: the spur is set by the residual detuning and is independent of β\betaβ (for a fixed detuning the kick must equal the drift); β\betaβ enters through how far the FLL / calibration can push Δf0\Delta f_0Δf0​ down, and through spur ∝β\propto\beta∝β when a fixed phase offset (e.g. a path-delay mismatch) is present.

5. Design takeaways​

5.1 Pulse width vs harmonic content​

Fixed area qinjq_{inj}qinj​: ∣IN∣=2qinjTinj∣sinc(f0τp)∣\vert I_N\vert=\dfrac{2q_{inj}}{T_{inj}}\big\vert\mathrm{sinc}(f_0\tau_p)\big\vert∣IN​∣=Tinj​2qinj​​​sinc(f0​τp​)​.

τp\tau_pτp​f0τpf_0\tau_pf0​τp​sinc\mathrm{sinc}sinc∣I20∣\vert I_{20}\vert∣I20​∣ (qinj=50q_{inj}=50qinj​=50 fC)
10 ps0.050.99624.90 μA
50 ps0.250.90022.51 μA
100 ps (T0/2T_0/2T0​/2)0.50.63715.92 μA
200 ps (T0T_0T0​)100

The null at τp=T0\tau_p=T_0τp​=T0​ has a physical meaning: the pulse spans a whole oscillation period, the positive and negative half-cycles of the ISF cancel, and the locking force vanishes — not "a wider pulse is slightly less efficient", a cliff. Design rule: τp≪T0\tau_p\ll T_0τp​≪T0​ (compared with the output period; larger NNN means shorter T0T_0T0​ and harder pulses — one of the hard limits of pushing ILCMs to high frequency). The fixed height IpI_pIp​ view (a current-limited driver): qinj=Ipτpq_{inj}=I_p\tau_pqinj​=Ip​τp​, ∣IN∣=2IpπNsin⁡(πf0τp)\vert I_N\vert=\frac{2I_p}{\pi N}\sin(\pi f_0\tau_p)∣IN​∣=πN2Ip​​sin(πf0​τp​), maximal at τp=T0/2\tau_p=T_0/2τp​=T0​/2 with 2Ip/(πN)2I_p/(\pi N)2Ip​/(πN) (Ip=5I_p=5Ip​=5 mA, N=20N=20N=20: 159 μA) — the kick efficiency is then 0.64, but the total charge is 10× larger. Both views say: make the pulse a small fraction of T0T_0T0​, but there is no need to push it to the limit — 10 ps already captures 99.6%.

The ring caveat (lab_40 (b)): the single sinc above holds only for "an ISF with just a fundamental". In general the kick is the box average of the ISF over the pulse window, and the mmm-th ISF harmonic is weighted by sinc(mf0τp)\mathrm{sinc}(mf_0\tau_p)sinc(mf0​τp​). A ring-type ISF concentrates its energy in triangular pulses about 1/f′1/f'1/f′ rad wide (Nst=17N_{st}=17Nst​=17 toy: 0.2460.2460.246 rad = 0.246/(2π)×2000.246/(2\pi)\times2000.246/(2π)×200 ps ≈7.8\approx7.8≈7.8 ps), so the pulse must also be narrower than that width: at the same 10 ps, the LC loses 0.4% while the ring toy's lock range drops to 0.68× (lab_40's unaveraged ODE agrees with the box-average prediction). A ring ILCM needs much narrower pulses than an LC — the flip side of the same node property as "rings win on qmaxq_{max}qmax​".

5.2 Ring vs LC​

Section 3's conclusion: β=(qinj/qmax) ∣Γ′(θss)∣\beta=(q_{inj}/q_{max})\,\vert\Gamma'(\theta_{ss})\vertβ=(qinj​/qmax​)∣Γ′(θss​)∣. The triangular ISF ties −sin⁡-\sin−sin on slope; the ring's advantage is all in qmaxq_{max}qmax​ (×100\times100×100). Practical meaning: a ring ILCM can run β∼0.5\beta\sim0.5β∼0.5–111 (nearly hard realignment every pulse, in-band almost purely reference), an LC only β∼10−2\beta\sim10^{-2}β∼10−2 (to stay in weak injection, and because a large qinjq_{inj}qinj​ kicks the amplitude). An LC ILCM relies on the oscillator being clean (small κ2\kappa^2κ2); a ring ILCM relies on frequent, forceful realignment. Section 5.4 quantifies this.

5.3 Choosing NNN (fixed f0f_0f0​)​

Write Section 4's two terms together (time-averaged; the full form for small β\betaβ):

␀σout2(N,β)=κ2NT0⋅1−β+β2/2β(2−β)⏟own: random walk between pulses ∝N+N2σψ2⋅β2−β⏟reference×N2\sigma_{out}^2(N,\beta)=\underbrace{\kappa^2NT_0\cdot\frac{1-\beta+\beta^2/2}{\beta(2-\beta)}}_{\text{own: random walk between pulses}\ \propto N} +\underbrace{N^2\sigma_\psi^2\cdot\frac{\beta}{2-\beta}}_{\text{reference}\times N^2}σout2​(N,β)=own: random walk between pulses ∝Nκ2NT0​⋅β(2−β)1−β+β2/2​​​+reference×N2N2σψ2​⋅2−ββ​​​
  • Own term ∝N\propto N∝N (σ∝N\sigma\propto\sqrt Nσ∝N​): the further apart the pulses, the further the random walk wanders.
  • Reference term: ×N2\times N^2×N2 in the phase domain; but in seconds, Nσψ/(2πf0)=σψ/(2πfref)=σt,refN\sigma_\psi/(2\pi f_0)=\sigma_\psi/(2\pi f_{ref})=\sigma_{t,ref}Nσψ​/(2πf0​)=σψ​/(2πfref​)=σt,ref​ — the reference's time jitter is passed 1:1 to the output, independent of NNN (rule 1 restated: ×N\times N×N in phase = the same seconds).
  • So for fixed f0f_0f0​ and fixed reference time jitter there is no interior optimum in NNN: smaller NNN is always better. With β\betaβ re-optimized for each NNN the script gives, for N=5,10,20,40,80N=5,10,20,40,80N=5,10,20,40,80, σt,min=5.99,7.12,8.46,10.07,11.97\sigma_{t,min}=5.99,7.12,8.46,10.07,11.97σt,min​=5.99,7.12,8.46,10.07,11.97 fs, log-log slope +0.250+0.250+0.250 — σt,min∝N1/4\sigma_{t,min}\propto N^{1/4}σt,min​∝N1/4 (small-β\betaβ closed form: σmin2≈σwNσψ\sigma_{min}^2\approx\sigma_w N\sigma_\psiσmin2​≈σw​Nσψ​, σw∝N\sigma_w\propto\sqrt Nσw​∝N​, NσψN\sigma_\psiNσψ​ fixed ⟹ ∝N1/2\propto N^{1/2}∝N1/2, then square-root). Doubling NNN costs only 19% more jitter — the noise penalty of NNN is mild.
  • What really limits NNN is elsewhere: (i) the lock range ∝1/N\propto1/N∝1/N (398 ppm at N=20N=20N=20) is far below PVT drift ⟹ an FLL is mandatory; (ii) the pulse must be ≪T0\ll T_0≪T0​; (iii) a clean, high-freff_{ref}fref​ reference costs money (if the reference is itself multiplied up from a crystal, Sref∝fref2S_{ref}\propto f_{ref}^2Sref​∝fref2​ and N2SrefN^2S_{ref}N2Sref​ is independent of NNN — same conclusion). If an "optimum NNN" exists it is a system-level cost/power optimum, not an extremum of this noise equation.

5.4 The β\betaβ trade-off: noise optimum vs lock range vs spur​

Extremize over β\betaβ (small β\betaβ: σw2/(2β)+N2σψ2β/2\sigma_w^2/(2\beta)+N^2\sigma_\psi^2\beta/2σw2​/(2β)+N2σψ2​β/2):

βopt≈σw2N2σψ2=σwNσψ,σout,min2≈σwNσψ\beta_{opt}\approx\sqrt{\frac{\sigma_w^2}{N^2\sigma_\psi^2}}=\frac{\sigma_w}{N\sigma_\psi},\qquad \sigma_{out,min}^2\approx\sigma_wN\sigma_\psiβopt​≈N2σψ2​σw2​​​=Nσψ​σw​​,σout,min2​≈σw​Nσψ​

— isomorphic to the "optimum loop bandwidth" of pll_noise_budget: VCO noise wants a wide loop, reference noise a narrow one.

Example 5 (βopt\beta_{opt}βopt​, assumed −160-160−160 dBc/Hz reference): LC: σw=22.4\sigma_w=22.4σw​=22.4 μrad, Nσψ=20×158N\sigma_\psi=20\times158Nσψ​=20×158 μrad ⟹ βopt=0.0071\beta_{opt}=0.0071βopt​=0.0071 (numerical minimization 0.00700.00700.0070), σout,min=8.46\sigma_{out,min}=8.46σout,min​=8.46 fs (16.3 fs at β=0.05\beta=0.05β=0.05); corresponding qinj,opt=7.07q_{inj,opt}=7.07qinj,opt​=7.07 fC, ΔfL=280\Delta f_L=280ΔfL​=280 kHz — a lock range too small to acquire frequency with; this is "the noise-optimal β\betaβ forces you to add an FLL". Ring (L(1 MHz)=−100\mathcal{L}(1\text{ MHz})=-100L(1 MHz)=−100 dBc/Hz ⟹ κ2=Sϕω2/2=3948\kappa^2=S_\phi\omega^2/2=3948κ2=Sϕ​ω2/2=3948 rad²/s, σw=3.97\sigma_w=3.97σw​=3.97 mrad = 126 fs per TinjT_{inj}Tinj​): βopt=0.695\beta_{opt}=0.695βopt​=0.695, σout,min=123\sigma_{out,min}=123σout,min​=123 fs; 395 fs at β=0.05\beta=0.05β=0.05, 135 fs at β=1\beta=1β=1 — the ring wants a large β\betaβ, and its small qmaxq_{max}qmax​ can afford it.

On the spur side (Section 4.4): at fixed detuning the spur is independent of β\betaβ; a larger β\betaβ does not worsen it, and a larger β\betaβ = larger lock range = an easier job for the FLL to squeeze Δf0\Delta f_0Δf0​. What really grows with β\betaβ is the pulse's direct coupling / AM disturbance (more visible as qinjq_{inj}qinj​ grows) — outside the first-order phase-only model, honestly left open.

5.6 Connection to SerDes​

Forwarded-clock architectures often take a low-rate forwarded clock (e.g. f0/4f_0/4f0​/4 or f0/8f_0/8f0​/8) and multiply it back to full rate at the receiver with an ILO / ILCM: this page's fcf_cfc​ is the jitter-tracking bandwidth — reference (forwarded-clock) jitter below fcf_cfc​ is copied onto the local clock (good for common jitter: transmitter and receiver correlate and cancel), above fcf_cfc​ the local oscillator is on its own (κ2\kappa^2κ2, i.e. the old Γrms/qmax\Gamma_{rms}/q_{max}Γrms​/qmax​ homework). The trade-off has the same structure as item 5 of injection_locking_noise and serdes_clocking_connection, only with N>1N\gt1N>1 and discrete updates.

6. Worked numbers: one Python block computes everything (canonical values)​

import numpy as np
f0, qmax, kappa2 = 5e9, 1e-12, 0.125          # Hz, C, rad^2/s (canonical)
N, qinj, tau_p = 20, 50e-15, 10e-12           # multiplication ratio, injected charge [C], pulse width [s]
fref = f0/N; Tinj = 1/fref                    # 250 MHz, 4 ns
I_N = 2*qinj/Tinj*abs(np.sinc(N*fref*tau_p))  # N-th injection harmonic amplitude [A] (sinc argument = f0*tau_p)
wL  = 0.5*I_N*(1/qmax)                        # route 1: (1/2)|I_N||Gt_1| [rad/s]
beta = qinj/qmax*abs(np.sinc(f0*tau_p))       # realignment factor (lock-range centre, incl. pulse width)
fc  = beta*fref/(2*np.pi*(1-beta))            # corner [Hz]
sw2 = kappa2*Tinj                             # phase variance accumulated per T_inj [rad^2]
var_avg = sw2*(1-beta+beta**2/2)/(beta*(2-beta))
S_ref = 2*10**(-160/10); sig_psi2 = S_ref*fref/2   # assumed -160 dBc/Hz white reference
var_ref = beta*N**2*sig_psi2/(2-beta)
b_opt = np.sqrt(sw2/(N**2*sig_psi2))
print(I_N*1e6)                                # -> 24.90 μA
print(wL, wL/2/np.pi/1e6)                     # -> 1.245e7 rad/s, 1.981 MHz
print(qinj/(qmax*Tinj)/2/np.pi/1e6)           # -> 1.989 MHz (impulse route, sinc=0.996 apart)
print(beta, -1/np.log(1-beta))                # -> 0.0498, 19.58 injections (to 1/e)
print(fc/1e6)                                 # -> 2.085 MHz
print(np.sqrt(var_avg)*1e6, np.sqrt(var_avg)/(2*np.pi*f0)*1e15)  # -> 69.99 μrad, 2.228 fs
print(10*np.log10(2*kappa2*Tinj**2/beta**2/2))                    # -> -150.9 dBc/Hz own-noise plateau
print(np.sqrt(var_ref)/(2*np.pi*f0)*1e15, 10*np.log10(N**2*S_ref/2))  # -> 16.08 fs, -134.0 dBc/Hz reference in-band
print(b_opt, b_opt*qmax*1e15)                 # -> 0.00707, 7.07 fC
print(20*np.log10(100e3/fref))                # -> -67.96 dBc (f_ref spur for a 100 kHz detuning)

(β=0.0498\beta=0.0498β=0.0498 includes the sinc of the 10 ps pulse; the table in Section 4 uses the delta train's β=0.05\beta=0.05β=0.05, 0.4% apart.)

Key takeaways​

  • [P4] writes out only the superharmonic Eq.(30); the subharmonic (multiplier) closed form follows from Eq.(29): selection rule k=mNk=mNk=mN, Ω(θ)=I0Γ~dc+12∑m∣Γ~m∣∣ImN∣cos⁡(mθ+⋯ )\Omega(\theta)=I_0\tilde\Gamma_{dc}+\tfrac12\sum_m\vert\tilde\Gamma_m\vert\vert I_{mN}\vert\cos(m\theta+\cdots)Ω(θ)=I0​Γ~dc​+21​∑m​∣Γ~m​∣∣ImN​∣cos(mθ+⋯), fundamental-dominated ωL=12∣IN∣∣Γ~1∣\omega_L=\tfrac12\vert I_N\vert\vert\tilde\Gamma_1\vertωL​=21​∣IN​∣∣Γ~1​∣. Division rides on ISF harmonics, multiplication on injection harmonics; a pure sinusoid at f0/Nf_0/Nf0​/N cannot lock to first order.
  • The arithmetic of [P3] footnote 7: one kick every NNN periods, ΔωL=qinj∣Γ~∣max/(NT0)∝1/N\Delta\omega_L=q_{inj}\vert\tilde\Gamma\vert_{max}/(NT_0)\propto1/NΔωL​=qinj​∣Γ~∣max​/(NT0​)∝1/N; a delta train's harmonics have equal weight ⟹ exactly equal to the Fourier route (Ω=qinjΓ~(θ)/Tinj\Omega=q_{inj}\tilde\Gamma(\theta)/T_{inj}Ω=qinj​Γ~(θ)/Tinj​). A finite pulse width multiplies by sinc(f0τp)\mathrm{sinc}(f_0\tau_p)sinc(f0​τp​) — compared with T0T_0T0​, not TinjT_{inj}Tinj​.
  • β=−qinjΓ~′(θss)\beta=-q_{inj}\tilde\Gamma'(\theta_{ss})β=−qinj​Γ~′(θss​): the fraction one pulse pulls back; stable for 0<β<20\lt\beta\lt20<β<2, settles in ≈1/β\approx1/\beta≈1/β injections; β/Tinj=ωc=−Ω′(θss)\beta/T_{inj}=\omega_c=-\Omega'(\theta_{ss})β/Tinj​=ωc​=−Ω′(θss​) (the pull-in frequency of [P3] Eq.(40)), =ΔωL=\Delta\omega_L=ΔωL​ for the LC at centre. The ring does not win on slope (the triangular toy ties at slope =1=1=1); it wins on a 100× smaller qmaxq_{max}qmax​.
  • Noise: Href=β/(1−(1−β)z−1)H_{ref}=\beta/(1-(1-\beta)z^{-1})Href​=β/(1−(1−β)z−1), Hosc=(1−z−1)/(1−(1−β)z−1)H_{osc}=(1-z^{-1})/(1-(1-\beta)z^{-1})Hosc​=(1−z−1)/(1−(1−β)z−1); in-band reference ×N2\times N^2×N2 (+26+26+26 dB at N=20N=20N=20), own-noise plateau 2κ2Tinj2/β22\kappa^2T_{inj}^2/\beta^22κ2Tinj2​/β2, corner ≈βfref/2π\approx\beta f_{ref}/2\pi≈βfref​/2π, out-of-band back to free-running (×1/(1−β)2\times1/(1-\beta)^2×1/(1−β)2). Closed-form output variance κ2NT0(1−β+β2/2)/(β(2−β))\kappa^2NT_0(1-\beta+\beta^2/2)/(\beta(2-\beta))κ2NT0​(1−β+β2/2)/(β(2−β)) (MC ratio 0.999; canonical 2.22 fs).
  • Spur: detuning sawtooth 20log⁡10(Δf0/fref)20\log_{10}(\Delta f_0/f_{ref})20log10​(Δf0​/fref​) (100 kHz → −68-68−68 dBc), first order, independent of β\betaβ.
  • Design: pulse width ≪T0\ll T_0≪T0​; βopt=σw/(Nσψ)\beta_{opt}=\sigma_w/(N\sigma_\psi)βopt​=σw​/(Nσψ​) is often so small that the lock range cannot cover PVT ⟹ add an FLL; the noise penalty of NNN is only N1/4N^{1/4}N1/4 — what limits NNN is the 1/N1/N1/N lock range, pulse speed and reference cost.
